### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **95** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/permission-set-row-definition.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/position-row-definition.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**44** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d231ba7876d0f420ecef280e57f8f9377ec7ac7`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/permission-set-row-definition.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/position-row-definition.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **151** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d231ba7876d0f420ecef280e57f8f9377ec7ac7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `758bc947f79b44e3c29bce0c053ba33a92ecfa19` — the merge of head `a338b13ce3566e73580f40a068ab9fad152e2198` into base `3d231ba7876d0f420ecef280e57f8f9377ec7ac7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 758bc947f79b44e3c29bce0c053ba33a92ecfa19 && git checkout 758bc947f79b44e3c29bce0c053ba33a92ecfa19
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3d231ba7876d0f420ecef280e57f8f9377ec7ac7 a338b13ce3566e73580f40a068ab9fad152e2198 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3d231ba7876d0f420ecef280e57f8f9377ec7ac7 && git merge --no-ff a338b13ce3566e73580f40a068ab9fad152e2198

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3d231ba7876d0f420ecef280e57f8f9377ec7ac7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3d231ba7876d0f420ecef280e57f8f9377ec7ac7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c4e9c4f919a2fff50b4473668203b312f8bfa079`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta review of PR #23428 (#22975 slice 8-post, `Fixes #22975`). The PR is a draft, and its head has not moved since the dispatch. The baseline is the FAIL record 6162274013 at `4366cc8e62`. The tree was read at 2026-10-14T10:25Z, with `origin/main` at `7b3d5585ca`.

How the delta was read:
- The old net diff is `5f852f064f..4366cc8e62`: 58 files, +420 / −2,305. The new net diff is `5656c5638a..c4e9c4f919`: 62 files, +480 / −2,290 = 2,770 lines.
- Each file's patch lines were compared across the two diffs. 12 files differ. The four files only in the new diff are among them: `protocol.ts`, `index.ts`, `position.mdx` and `permission.mdx`.
- The merge `d817abfad6`, against an automatic merge of its two parents, differs only in its four conflicted files:
  - the two census files and `packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts` take main's side, and none of the three is in the net diff;
  - `packaged-permission-set-overlay-detection.ts` keeps a net patch identical to the old one.

Inputs read: the record 6162274013, the dispatch 6148409420, the seat's answers 6161961558, the dev's reports 6163844068 and 6165992713, and the claim 6120370976. Also the PR body (updated 2026-10-14T10:13Z), its file list, the net diff and the delta, ADR-0131 D3 and D13 on `origin/main`, the 41 check-runs on the head, #23403, #23404 and #23412. Every suite count and every ablation is the dev's claim. Nothing was built, run or re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Item 1, which was blocking, is fixed. No live-code pin is deleted anywhere in the net diff.**
- **The describe is back, byte-identical.** `DelegatedAdminGate — direct grants (sys_user_permission_set)` is 80 lines with the same sha256 (`c91f80506a64b754…`) at `dac99c2277`, at `5656c5638a`, at `origin/main` and at the head. It holds all nine cases: four top-level cases and the five in `[ADR-0131 D4] the pre-image is judged by the name the grant holds`.
- **Every case still exercises live code** (`delegated-admin-gate.ts` at the head):
  - `assert` dispatches `sys_user_permission_set` to `assertDirectGrantWrite` (`:399`–`400`), which reads each row through `directGrantSet` (`:808`, `:1121`).
  - The refusals the cases match are all emitted there: "outside the delegated subtree" (`:822`), "not in the scope's allowlist" (`:816`), "not strictly contained" (`assertScopeGrantContainment`, `:870`), "names no permission set" (`:1136`) and "is not in the security catalog" (`:1144`).
  - `GOVERNED_OBJECTS` keeps `sys_user_permission_set`.
- **The `granted_by` case:** it loses only its `sys_position_permission_set` half. That half pinned the binding branch this PR deletes, and the `sys_member` half stays. This was the previous record's non-blocking item, and it is done.
- **Every other deleted case pins code that is deleted here.** That holds for the two-doors, system-row and curated-name describes, the three `store-fault-fail-closed` describes, the blast-radius describe, the boot test's dangling-name case and the `FLOOR` entry. The delta changes no other test file's patch.

**2. Items 3, 5 and 6 are done. Two statements are false on main plus this PR, and one of them ships.**
- **Item 3:** `PermissionSet.description`'s doc comment now reads "Human-readable description of the set." The reader clause is gone.
- **Item 5:** every named place is fixed, and each new example is true on the head:
  - `delegated-admin-gate.ts:865`, `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts:37`–`45` (now past tense), `index.ts:125`–`126` and `error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1257` ("a metadata-door save").
  - In `protocol.ts`, the publish materializer is service-automation's `flow` materializer (`plugin.ts:888`), and the mutation projector is service-datasource's `datasource` projector (`datasource-admin-plugin.ts:624`). The uninstall cleanup revokes grants, and `cleanupPackagePermissions` returns `userGrants + suggestions`.
  - The checklist item's title now names the retired data door. Its `automated.ref` names `packaged-permission-set-lock.test.ts` and `packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.test.ts`, and both exist.
- **Item 6 (Q4):** both describes now read "unique within the security catalog the environment serves".
  - This matches D3 ("There is **no organization-level catalog**"), and the execution-plan note's item 1 ("Under `single` a position name is unique per deployment").
  - The rendered reference rows equal the describe strings. The reference-docs sync step (`check:docs`, in Type Check · source gates) is green on the head.
- **False on main plus this PR, and blocking before the queue:**
  - The changeset says: "The audience-anchor binding gate on `sys_position_permission_set` stays for now, unchanged; an accepted ADR still names it, and it leaves with that record's correction."
  - #23412 (`be50633be1`) deleted the gate and corrected ADR-0138. Its own changeset, `23403-audience-anchor-binding-gate-retired.md`, says the gate is deleted.
  - Merged, the two changesets would put contradictory lines into `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s release notes.
- **Non-blocking prose misses, in the same family:**
  - **`protocol.ts`:** three docblocks still give `sys_permission_set` as the live example:
    - `UninstallCleanup` (`:5745`–`5748`), an entry-exported type whose doc ships in d.ts;
    - `MetadataMutationProjector` (`:5982`–`5984`), also entry-exported;
    - the save path's projection comment (`:22608`–`22609`).

    Three more comments call `sys_permission_set` "the shipped case" of a delete reset through plugin-security's write-through: `:14646`, `:15847` and `:16507`.
  - **`security-plugin.ts:4381`–`4385`:** the comment at the cleanup's registration says the cleanup removes "package-owned sets + their position/user bindings". The sweep has no row leg left: `sets` and `positionBindings` are always 0.
  - **`delegated-admin-gate.ts:110`–`111` and `delegated-admin-gate-holding-organization.test.ts:9`–`10`:** both say "`sys_position.name` is unique per organization only" in the present tense. That now contradicts this PR's own D3 restatement. The PR rewrote the very next lines of that test header and left this one.
  - **Wording nit, optional:** "unique within the security catalog" can be read as unique across item types. A position may share a name with a set or a capability (the deleted curated-name scope-control case pinned exactly that). "Among the catalog's positions" would be exact.
  - **Still open from the previous record, never on the closing list:**
    - `catalog-reference-report.ts:33`'s heading "Positions naming no permission set";
    - the fallback warning at `security-plugin.ts:4534`, which names only assignments and grants.

**3. Nothing else the delta touches breaks a "right" finding of the previous record.**
- **The 12 delta files:** the changeset, `position.mdx`, `permission.mdx`, `access-security.json`, `protocol.ts`, `delegated-admin-gate.test.ts`, `delegated-admin-gate.ts`, `index.ts`, `packaged-permission-set-lock.ts`, `error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, `position.zod.ts` and `permission.zod.ts`. Every hunk is prose, the restored tests, or the regenerated rows.
  - The `packageId` hunk in `4366cc8e62..c4e9c4f919` is main's, not this PR's: the net diff does not touch that hunk.
- **The 7a merge:**
  - `protocol.mdx` was regenerated by `3f06e9d140`, and its net patch is the same 6 lines as before.
  - `proof-registry.mts` has no `permission-set-projection` entry.
  - The `protocol.ts` uninstall-cleanup comments the dev added are true, but incomplete: they omit the suggestion rows.
- **The previous right findings are unchanged:**
  - **The walled data door's retirement, the sixth catalog-report class and every re-tightened span** have patches identical to the old ones.
  - **The walled door still guards nothing on `origin/main`.** No non-test object definition declares `sys_position`, `sys_permission_set` or `sys_capability`. The merged tree names none of the door's three symbols.
  - **The handler floors still hold.** The merged tree still registers exactly two `kernel:bootstrapped` handlers (`security-plugin.ts:4547` and `:4561`), after #23433's move of the built-in declarations into `init()`.
  - **The sixth class should stay quiet on a fresh boot.** Since #23433, `init()` declares `everyone` naming `member_default`. The report test's harness declares `defaultPermissionSets`, so that name resolves. This is NOT MEASURED on the merged tree.
- **Keeping `assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate` is overtaken by `main`.** The merge must take main's deletion (item 4).

**4. The merge state: the head CONFLICTS with `main`.**
- **The conflict:** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main refs/review/pr-23428` gives `CONFLICT (content)` in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`, in two hunks: the middleware call sites, and the gate bodies.
  - It is unchanged at `7b3d5585ca`, the newest main, whose three latest commits touch no file of this PR.
  - REST reads `mergeable: false` and `mergeable_state: dirty`, three times over.
- **The resolution is unambiguous: drop both sides.**
  - Main's side holds only the three gates this PR deletes: `assertPackageManagedWriteGate`, `assertSystemRowWriteGate` with `SYSTEM_ROW_PROVENANCE`, and `assertCuratedCapabilityNameGate`. The PR's side holds only the anchor gate that #23412 deleted.
  - Checked on the merge-tree output: dropping both sides gives a file whose diff against `main` is the PR's own net patch for that file, line for line, up to the diff's alignment of blank and brace lines.
  - That file names no symbol that this PR or #23412 deletes. `AnchorBindingContext` and `readDeclaredCapabilityContext` stay in use by #23433's `everyoneBaseline`.
- ⛔ **Keeping the PR side** would re-add a gate whose import `describeAnchorForbiddenBits` main has removed, and the tree would not compile.
- **Every other overlapping file merges by itself.** That covers `security-plugin.test.ts`, `access-security.json`, `protocol.ts`, `grant-permission-set-name-backfill.test.ts` and `object-posture-gate.ts`.
- **The PR adds no reference to the removed gate.** Its only other mention in the tree is main's own `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts:360` (③).
- **No CI has run on the merged combination.** The head's CI ran on the merge ref at 2026-10-14T08:15Z. `be50633be1` landed at 2026-10-14T08:18Z. So no CI has seen this PR together with #23412, #23433, #23441, #23408 or #23411, and none can until the branch merges `main`.
- **This record will not carry to the merged head.** The hand resolution and the changeset edit are this PR's own paths, so record-recognisers' regen-carry refuses them. A delta review of the merge follows.

### ② Semver level

- **The delta adds `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`.** It changes doc comments only. Those ship in d.ts, but they are no accept set, key or export. Patch.
- **`@objectstack/spec`:** in the delta, two describe strings and their comments. No key, value, type or export moves. Patch.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-security`:** in the delta, the `index.ts` comment and two prose edits in source. The rest is test restoration. Patch.
- **The delta does not change the published surface.** Under WHICH LEVEL, nothing widens an index or an accept set, so patch is the level, and `fix(` does not lower it. `Clause-②: no` is right, and the level axis of `check-changeset-no-major` stands down for an undeclared clause.
- **The rest of the levels stand from the previous record,** because their patches are unchanged. The one sentence to drop is in ①2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on the head:** 41, all completed and none running. 35 succeeded and 5 were skipped: Console Pin Gate, the sharded Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, the packed-tarball smoke and Temporal Conformance.
- **One check failed:** "The card this PR closes must claim this branch". Its annotation reads: "PR #23428 closes #22975 with no `Claim:` on the card naming `claude/issue-22975-8post-recut`".
  - The claim 6120370976 names `claude/issue-22975-8post`. It says itself that "The PR that closes the card gets a fresh `Claim:` naming its branch", and none has been posted.
  - The seat posts that claim and re-runs the check.
- **The deviations in report 6163844068:**
  - The wrong dogfood filter was refused, and nothing ran. Answered: no effect.
  - The worktree is kept. Answered: remove it at landing.
- **The out-of-scope findings in 6163844068:**
  - **The `access-security` item.** Answered. Its title and `automated.ref` are fixed. Its other clauses record the flow of a `status: retired` item, which has a `retiredReason`, so no carrier is needed.
  - **The `deletePackage` comment.** Answered: fixed in this round.
  - **`manageBindings` and `authorEnvironmentSets`.** Escalated: still unfiled. It is the seat's own item from the closing list, filed at landing.
- **The deviations in report 6165992713:**
  - The round landed on the open PR. Answered: the PR is a draft and was never queued, so no effect.
  - The uninstall-cleanup comments go beyond the list. Answered: in scope, comments only, and true (①3).
  - The four body corrections are all applied in the current body.
- **Body claims the code contradicts:**
  - "**Kept, unchanged:** `SecurityPlugin.assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate`…" and "Carried, not in this PR: #23403". #23403 was closed by #23412, and the gate is gone on `main`.
  - "the publish-materializer, mutation-projector and uninstall-cleanup comments in `protocol.ts` give the examples registered today". `protocol.ts:5748`, `:5984` and `:22609` contradict it. The changeset's narrower "registries" is accurate.
  - "`packages/spec` is touched in describe text and doc comments only". The PR also removes the `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` row from the exported `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER`, which the body's own What-changes section states.
  - "Verification: … `origin/main` `5656c5638a` merged once". True of the head, but `main` has moved since, and the head conflicts.
- **Needs a carrier:**
  - `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts:360` (on `main`) says the deleted `assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate` "enforces the same rules on the binding write". #23412 missed it. It is the "showcase guest-binding doc" that the old report marked carrier none, and no card holds it. Fold it into the merge, or file a card.
  - ADR-0090 D9 and D12 are NOT MEASURED. They go to the seat's enforce-or-remove card at landing.
  - #23404 is open and carries `permission.json:20`.
- **NOT MEASURED: the spec suite's 4 red files.**
  - `content/docs/protocol-upgrade/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:114`) and generated at the docs build. No copy is committed, so CI's checkout for Test Core lacks it.
  - All six Test Core shards are green on this head. Spec is a touched package, so `ci.yml`'s affected-set rule puts it in a shard. The shard logs were not read, because the proxy refused the log host.
  - So CI agrees as far as it can be seen: a local artefact, not a gate. Whether the same 4 go red locally on `main` is not shown, because the dev reports no run on `main`.
- **NOT MEASURED: the rest.**
  - Dogfood: PR CI skips the shards, so the count is the dev's claim only.
  - The objectui pinned sibling: Console Pin Gate was skipped.
  - `check:platform-checklist`'s 8 reds: the gate is out of per-PR CI, so this is the dev's claim.
  - `check-engine-split-ratio`'s local exit 2: CI's engine-gates lane is green.
  - The merged tree: nothing has built or tested `main` plus this PR.

**The patch round, all before the queue:**
1. Merge `origin/main`, and resolve `security-plugin.ts` by dropping both sides. Then run the final gates on the new head.
2. Drop the changeset's anchor-gate sentence. Correct the body's "Kept, unchanged", "#23403" and "Verification" lines.
3. The seat posts a fresh `Claim:` on #22975 naming `claude/issue-22975-8post-recut`, and re-runs the claim check.
4. A delta review of the merge follows.

The prose misses in ①2 are optional.

**Seat adoption** (2026-10-14T10:27Z). Adopted after an audit of the reviewer transcript: one Write, to this record only; 94 Bash calls, all reads (`git show`, `git diff`, `git merge-tree`, REST GETs); no MCP call, no GitHub write, no worktree, build or test run. The seat re-ran `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main refs/review/pr-23428`: exit 1, a conflict. The seat rules:
- **Item 1:** merge `main` now. A conflict is one of the three reasons ruling #23390 allows. Resolve `security-plugin.ts` by dropping both sides, as the record describes.
- **Items 2, 3 and 6:** fix them in the merge push. Drop the changeset's "stays for now" sentence; correct the three body lines and the `protocol.ts` claim; fix `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts:360`. The optional prose rides the same push.
- **Item 4:** the seat posts a fresh `Claim:` on #22975 naming `claude/issue-22975-8post-recut`, as claim 6120370976 says the closing PR gets.
- **Item 5:** the merged head gets its own delta review, scoped to the merge resolution and this push, with the CI of that head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a338b13ce3566e73580f40a068ab9fad152e2198`
Local-runs: none

This is a scoped delta review of PR #23428 (#22975 slice 8-post, `Fixes #22975`) after its merge of `main`. The head is `a338b13ce3`, the head the brief named; it has not moved. The baseline is the FAIL record 6166282376 at `c4e9c4f919`. The tree was read at 2026-10-14T11:51Z, with `origin/main` at `3d231ba787`. The merge state and the check-runs were read again at 2026-10-14T12:22Z, with `origin/main` at `1baf976cf9`.

How the delta was read:
- **The two net diffs.** The old one is `5656c5638a...c4e9c4f919`: 62 files. The new one is `7b3d5585ca...a338b13ce3`: 63 files, +514 / −2,322. Each file's patch lines were compared across the two.
- **56 files have identical patches.** 7 differ: the changeset, `examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts` (new to the diff), `protocol.ts`, `catalog-reference-report.ts`, `delegated-admin-gate.ts`, `delegated-admin-gate-holding-organization.test.ts` and `security-plugin.ts`. Each difference is exactly `a33c341826`'s prose edit, plus `a338b13ce3`'s four-line deletion in `security-plugin.ts`.
- **The merge.** The merge is `f3d19d8279`, with parents `c4e9c4f919` and `7b3d5585ca` (the brief's `7b3d5585ca` is the main tip it merged). Its tree differs from `git merge-tree --write-tree` of its parents only in the one conflicted file, `security-plugin.ts`.

Inputs read: the record 6166282376 (items 1 to 6 and the seat adoption), the dev's report 6167515372 and the claim 6166295001. Also the PR body (updated 2026-10-14T11:50Z), its file list, the net diff and the delta, and the head's check-runs: 38 at the first read, 41 when the run finished. #23403's state and `be50633be1`'s file list were read to check two body lines. Every suite count is the dev's claim. Nothing was built, run or re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The merge resolution is right at the head. The merge commit itself left an orphan, and `a338b13ce3` removes it.**
- **The conflict.** The automatic merge of the two parents conflicts only in `security-plugin.ts`, in two hunks:
  - the middleware call sites: the anchor gate's call on the PR side, the three gates' calls on main's side;
  - the gate bodies: `assertAudienceAnchorBindingGate` on the PR side, and on main's side `assertPackageManagedWriteGate`, `assertSystemRowWriteGate` with the `PACKAGE_POSITION_*` helpers, and `assertCuratedCapabilityNameGate`.

  Both sides are dropped in both hunks.
- **The orphan in `f3d19d8279`.** The context the two sides of the second hunk shared stayed behind: a `/**` above the hunk, and `    }` / `  }` below it. That opener swallowed the two braces up to the next docblock's `*/`. The merge commit's file has 155 `/*` against 154 `*/`, and a nested opener at `:6758`. The two stray braces sat inside that comment, so no code token moved.
- **The fix.** `a338b13ce3` deletes exactly those four lines (`/**`, `    }`, `  }`, a blank). At the head:
  - `/*` and `*/` balance at 154 each.
